title: headwater-calc/3
description: Printed by `headwater calc --json`: the scores of each product of a database or a study, for each indicator, with provenance. Example, in the folder of `headwater demo`: `headwater calc project/tshirt-footprint --json`.

path.description: The database or study folder, as given.

name.description: The name of the database or the study.

release.description: The release the background was read from, as name@hash. Null for a folder.

folder.description: The folder the background was read from. Null for a release.

background.description: The background the scores are calculated on.

method.description: The method the background was loaded with, and the hash of its content. Null when several methods are used together: `methods` names them.

methods.description: The id of each method the background was loaded with, in order.

engine_version.description: The version of headwater that calculated the scores.

solver.description: How the background was factorized. The database's own processes use the same settings.

scenario.description: The scenario of the study the scores are calculated in, from `--scenario`. Null for none.

id.description: The id of the process that makes the product.

flow.description: The id of the flow the process makes.

unit.description: The unit of that flow. Null when the flow has no record.

amount.description: For a study only: how much of the product it scores, in `unit`.

per.description: What each score is for: `1 kg` for a database, the amount and unit of a study's product, `0.5 kg`. Null when `unit` is null.

input_hash.description: sha256 of the inputs the product's scores are calculated from.

residual.description: The largest residual of the solves behind the product's scores.

cancels.description: The indicators whose score is near 0 because its positive and negative parts cancel. For a database only the first product is calculated in full, so it is null for the others.

products.description: Each product scored. For a database, the first is calculated in full and the others are scored on the same background.

unit.description: The unit of the score. Empty for a normalised score.

score.description: For a study, the score of its amount of the product.

results.description: One score per product and indicator.

pin.description: The background the database or the study pins, as written: `toy-background@6864b7dbb65d`.

uses.description: For a database, the databases it uses, directly or not, by name. For a study, every database it reaches.

condition.description: The condition estimate of the factors the background was solved with. For a database, the first product's. For a study, the largest of its products.

database_condition.description: The same estimate for the block of the database's own processes. For a database, the first product's. For a study, the largest of its products.

residual.description: The largest residual of every product.

processes.description: Every process that emits or takes the flow.

reason.description: For a flow of a database's own processes, the reason its `no_factor.csv` row gives. Null otherwise.

not_characterised.description: The elementary flows the method has no factor for, in any indicator, each once. They count 0 in every score. For a database, those of the first product. For a study, those of every product.

database.description: For a database only: the database, and the commit its git repository is at, null when it is not in git. `changed` is true when its files, or those of a database it uses, differ from that commit.

study.description: For a study only: the study, and the commit its git repository is at, null when it is not saved or not in git. `changed` is true when its files, or those of a database it reaches, differ from that commit.
